questions.questionText:
Which row shows the best choice of measuring instruments to obtain accurate values for the
distances shown?
diameter of wire height of bench length of laboratory

options.text: measuring tape measuring tape micrometer screw gauge
metre rule micrometer measuring tape screw gauge
micrometer measuring tape metre rule screw gauge
micrometer metre rule measuring tape screw gauge

questions.questionText:
An object is moving with uniform deceleration.
Which statement describes its motion?

options.text: Its rate of change of speed is decreasing.
Its speed is constant.
Its speed is decreasing.
Its speed is increasing.

questions.questionText:
The gravitational field strength on the Moon is less than on the Earth.
Which of these is different when done on the Moon compared with when done on the Earth?

options.text: the gravitational potential energy gained by a stone lifted through the same vertical height
the kinetic energy gained by a ball when hit with the same force for the same period of time
the momentum gained by a bullet when fired from the same gun
the work done in accelerating a stone from rest to the same speed

questions.questionText: Which moving body has a resultant force acting on it?

options.text: a diver rising vertically through water at constant speed
an aircraft circling an airport at constant speed
a train going up a straight incline at constant speed
a parachutist descending vertically at terminal velocity

questions.questionText:
A constant force acts on a body causing the momentum of the body to increase.
Which expression relates the force to the momentum and the time taken?
change in momentum

options.text: force = time taken momentum
force = time taken
force = change in momentum × time taken
force = momentum × time taken

questions.questionText: Which source of energy uses the production of steam to generate electrical energy?

options.text: hydroelectric
nuclear
tides
waves

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a U-tube manometer containing three liquids: mercury, liquid X and liquid Y.
Neither liquid X or liquid Y mixes with mercury.
liquid X liquid Y
mercury
Which row compares the pressure exerted by liquid X and by liquid Y on the mercury, and the
density of liquid X and the density of liquid Y?
pressure exerted by X and densities of
by Y on the mercury X and of Y

options.text: pressure of X is greater than Y density of X is greater than Y
pressure of Y is greater than X density of Y is greater than X
pressure of X and of Y is the same density of X is greater than Y
pressure of X and of Y is the same density of Y is greater than X

questions.questionText:
Gas molecules exert a pressure when they collide with the walls of a container.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: They experience a change in force which exerts a pressure equal to momentum × area on the walls. momentum
They experience a change in force which exerts a pressure equal to on the area walls.
They experience a change in momentum which exerts a pressure equal to force × area on the walls. force
They experience a change in momentum which exerts a pressure equal to on the area walls.

questions.questionText:
A thermometer has graduations which start at –10°C and end at 110°C.
–10 0 100 110
What is the lower fixed point and what is the upper fixed point of the Celsius scale?
lower fixed point upper fixed point
/°C /°C

A 1kg block of aluminium requires more thermal energy to raise its temperature by 1°C than a
1kg block of copper requires.
Why is this?

options.text: Aluminium is a better conductor of thermal energy than copper.
Aluminium is a poorer conductor of thermal energy than copper.
Aluminium has a higher specific heat capacity than copper.
Aluminium has a lower specific heat capacity than copper.

questions.questionText:
Four campers are warming their food on a fire.
They use different rods, each of the same dimensions, to hold their food near the fire.
rod
food
fire
Which material is the best choice to prevent their hands from getting too hot?

options.text: aluminium
copper
steel
wood

questions.questionText:
Two metal cans are identical, except that one has a shiny silver outer surface and the other has a
dull black outer surface. They each have 300g of water at 80°C sealed inside them. They are
both in a vacuum, in the darkness of outer space.
How does the temperature of the water in each one change?

options.text: Neither one will cool down.
The water in the black can cools more slowly than that in the shiny can.
The water in the shiny can cools more slowly than that in the black can.
They both cool down at the same rate.

questions.questionText:
What is the speed of X-rays in a vacuum and in air?
in a vacuum in air

The ends of three metal rods are tested by holding end Q of rod 1 close to the others in turn.
R T
Q S U
rod 1 rod 2 rod 3
The results are as follows.
End Q attracts end R.
End Q attracts end S.
End Q attracts end T.
End Q repels end U.
Which of the metal rods is a magnet?

options.text: rod 1 only
rod 1 and rod 2
rod 1 and rod 3
rod 3 only

questions.questionText:
A metal sphere is charged by induction. There are four stages W, X, Y and Z in this process.
W a charged rod is brought near to the sphere
X the sphere is earthed
Y the charged rod is taken away from the sphere
Z the earth connection is removed
In which order are the four stages carried out?

options.text: W → X → Y → Z
W → X → Z → Y
Z → W → X → Y
X → Z → W → Y

questions.questionText:
Which electrical quantity is defined in terms of the energy supplied in driving charge round a
complete circuit?

options.text: current
electromotive force
potential difference
power

questions.questionText:
The current in a kettle is 10A and the kettle is protected by a 13A fuse.
The owner of the kettle replaces the 13A fuse with a 3A fuse.
What happens when the kettle is switched on?

options.text: The fuse melts and the kettle might be damaged.
The fuse melts and the kettle is undamaged.
The fuse does not melt and the kettle works correctly.
The fuse does not melt but the kettle fails to work.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the direction of a magnetic field at a point is correct?

options.text: It is the direction of the force on a north pole placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on a south pole placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on a positive charge placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on a negative charge placed at that point.

questions.questionText:
A current-carrying coil is placed in a magnetic field.
view from above
coil magnetic field lines
Which effect does the coil experience?

options.text: a change in shape
a change in weight
a resultant force
a turning effect

questions.questionText: What are isotopes of an element?

options.text: atoms of a different element with a different number of neutrons
atoms of a different element with a different number of protons
atoms of the same element with a different number of neutrons
atoms of the same element with a different number of protons

questions.questionText:
A radioactive isotope of carbon 14C decays by beta emission to give an isotope of nitrogen 14N
and a beta particle. The equation for the reaction is shown.
14C → 14N + 0β
X 7 Y
What is the value of X and of Y?
X Y

A beta particle is a fast moving electron.
Which statement explains how beta particles are emitted from an atom?

options.text: An electron is emitted as a beta particle from an inner electron shell of the atom.
An electron is emitted as a beta particle from an outer electron shell of the atom.
A neutron changes into a proton and a beta particle is emitted from the nucleus.

A proton changes into a neutron and a beta particle is emitted from the nucleus.
